title: With de la Place: the dependence cannot be too great, so long as God is not made author of sin; immediate concurrence most probable
source_text: LVII. Sed modo Deus author peccati non constituatur, cum Doctissimo Placeo, judico causarum secundarum in agendo dependentiam a prima nimiam statui non posse. Et maxime quoque mihi probabile videtur Deum, juxta communem Scholarum sententiam, ad omnes & singulos creaturarum actus immediate concurrere.
pass_a_gloss: But provided God be not made the author of sin, with the most Learned de la Place, I judge that the dependence of second causes in acting on the first cannot be laid down too great. And it seems to me also most probable that God, according to the common opinion of the Schools, concurs immediately to all and each of the acts of creatures.
pass_b_english: But as long as God is not made the author of sin, I judge with the most learned de la Place that the dependence of secondary causes on the first in their acting cannot be made too great.
It also seems to me highly probable that God, as the Schools commonly hold, concurs immediately in each and every act of creatures.

lemmas.gloss: cannot be laid down too great

choices.why: The Schools' term for God's acting together with secondary causes; 'concurrence' keeps it recognizable as the technical term, with 'cooperation' kept for cooperatio.
